text_blocks.snippet: State and local agencies warn that residents in Central Illinois are frequently targeted by fake text messages from scammers impersonating the Illinois Secretary of State or Illinois Department of Transportation. These phishing texts falsely claim recipients owe money for unpaid traffic violations or tolls, threatening immediate license or registration suspension.
Common Scam Trends in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Fake Traffic and Toll Texts: Messages claiming unpaid fines with malicious payment links. State offices never text to demand payment.
Package Delivery Phishing: Texts from fake couriers claiming a package cannot be delivered due to a missing house number, prompting users to click a link.
Impersonation and AI Scams: Fraudsters posing as family members, government officials, or tech support using urgent language to demand money.
Post-Disaster and Charity Fraud: Phony contractors or fake charities soliciting funds or bank information following severe weather or emergencies.
Do not click links in unexpected text messages or emails regarding fines or package deliveries.

Practice the pause
by taking time to independently verify urgent claims through official organization numbers rather than provided contacts.
Never share personal data or bank account numbers over the phone or via unverified web forms.
